decisions.reason: The orthogonality argument is correct only after identifying the zero weight space with the Cartan subalgebra, and its cited decomposition expressly assumes Choice. The carrier omitted that hypothesis and left the identification unstated; both are now explicit.

The listed complex-linear properties did not by themselves supply the real Euclidean ambient space and positive-definite form required by the title. The repair constructs the real Cartan form, proves positivity, and identifies the orthogonal reflection formula.

Finiteness of the root set was imported from a theorem whose interface assumes Choice, while the definition stated it unconditionally. The definition now exposes the same axiom and declares its direct dependency.

The eigenspace decomposition and regular-set interface both carry an explicit Choice hypothesis, but the proposition omitted it. The formula is valid after propagating that hypothesis and declaring the axiom dependency.

The decomposition and Cartan-structure facts used in the proof have explicit Choice hypotheses, whereas the proposition had none. The mathematical kernel argument is sound once the missing axiom is propagated.

The maximal-abelian counterexample itself was valid, but the carrier additionally called the ambient algebra nonsemisimple without support. The repair proves that CY is a nonzero solvable ideal and hence lies in the radical.

The defining formula was correct, but its explanatory sentence falsely treated a_ij as an eigenvalue on alpha_j. In general the reflected root is not collinear with alpha_j; a_ij is the alpha_i coefficient subtracted.

The Cartan/maximal-toral theorem could not be applied until the direct sum was proved semisimple, and the cited definitions did not supply radical additivity. The repair proves both radical inclusions using componentwise derived series and projections.

A vector-space basis of coroots does not alone license a based Cartan matrix. The repair first proves the dual root-system axioms, then uses the common chamber facets and reducedness to prove that the simple roots of the dual are exactly the simple coroots.

The statement assigned the two dimensions in the reverse order even though its proof computed them correctly. Trace-zero diagonal matrices in sl_n have dimension n-1, while the three form-preserving families have dimension n.

The dimension count required equality between Cartan dimension and root-system rank, but the original facts only named Lie rank and a root-system isomorphism. The repair cites and explains the real-form identification that proves the needed equality.

The cited classification theorems are restricted to finite-dimensional complex simple and semisimple Lie algebras, but the remark omitted that qualifier. Its intended contrast with real forms and global groups remains correct after narrowing the claim.

The conclusion claimed the complete low-rank range n at most 2, but the proof only handled n=2. The missing n=1 case is now checked directly: multiplication by two maps {plus-or-minus e_1} onto {plus-or-minus 2e_1} and preserves the A1 Cartan integer.

Fact L2 omitted the supplier's empty rank-zero irreducible case. The main proof already establishes that a simple algebra has a nonempty root system before using L2, so qualifying L2 by nonempty repairs the inaccurate restatement without changing the classification argument.

The carrier computed the coordinate root sets but identified their types by reaching into the proof of an existence theorem whose public interface only promised realizations. The repair independently exhibits bases, positive-root expansions, Cartan matrices, and low-rank isomorphisms.

The Serre presentation supplier is conditional on chosen simple-root sl_2 triples, but the carrier simply chose them without an existence result. The repair adds the root-triple theorem and separates existence from the conditional presentation isomorphism.

The explicit cycle calculation correctly refuted the stated universal claim, but the final sentence asserted a general tree lemma that was neither a dependency nor proved. The repair removes that overreach and strengthens the null-vector argument against every diagonal conjugate.

The Given clause wrote the coordinate model in alpha and beta but then introduced unrelated alpha_0 and beta_0, so the proof's substitution was not licensed and even obscured the coefficient swap. The model and renaming are now stated consistently.

Step 1.4 used simple-arm equal-length expansions before the proof had excluded other multiple edges. Its conditional sublemma now expressly assumes a unique multiple edge that is double; step 3.1 establishes exactly those hypotheses before invoking it.

reviews.reason: The repaired statement assumes Choice, declares the axiom dependency, and records g_0=h before treating the zero-weight case; invariance then proves orthogonality and nondegeneracy exactly as claimed.

The proof now builds h_R from Lie coroots, proves h=h_R direct-sum i h_R, computes the Killing trace as a positive sum of squares, transports it to span_R Phi, and verifies reflection and crystallographic axioms.

The definition now assumes Choice at its public interface and cites the axiom directly, so its finite-union assertion is licensed by the repaired root-system theorem under exactly matching hypotheses.

With Choice explicit, the direct-sum eigenvalue computation gives exactly the kernel summands, one-dimensionality gives the root count, and the repaired regular-set definition gives the final equivalence.

The repaired interface assumes Choice directly; root-space decomposition plus abelianness makes the common kernel central, centerlessness makes it zero, and finite-dimensional duality yields spanning of h-star.

The calculation now verifies CY is an abelian nonzero ideal, so the radical is nonzero and the algebra is nonsemisimple; the normalizer computations for CY and CX remain correct and complete the counterexample.
The definition now correctly identifies a_ij as the coefficient of alpha_i in alpha_j minus its reflection and explicitly warns that it is not generally an eigenvalue of alpha_j.

The proof now derives rad(g1 direct-sum g2)=rad(g1) direct-sum rad(g2), obtains semisimplicity before invoking maximal-toral structure, and then verifies the Cartan decomposition and root union componentwise.

The repaired proof verifies dual reflection stability and integrality, identifies the dual base through the unchanged Weyl chamber facets, and only then computes the transposed Cartan matrix and reversed arrows.
The public statement now matches the verified diagonal parameter counts: C^(n-1) for sl_n and C^n for sp_2n, so_2n, and so_(2n+1); the normalizer and maximal-toral proof remains sound.
The proof now uses the repaired Lie-root theorem to identify dim_C h with dim_R span_R Phi, uses root-system isomorphism to preserve this rank, and then adds the verified exceptional root counts.

The remark now says finite-dimensional in both classification clauses and declares its inherited Choice assumption directly; the limitations concerning real forms and global group topology are unchanged.

The long/short-root cardinality obstruction still proves nonisomorphism for n at least 3, while the proof now separately establishes B_1 isomorphic to C_1 and retains the cited B_2 isomorphic to C_2 case.
L2 now exactly says nonempty irreducible systems have the displayed types and records the supplier's empty-system convention; step 1.1 independently excludes the empty case for simple Lie algebras.

The proof now derives the A, B, C, and D simple bases from explicit positive-root expansions, computes every nontrivial terminal Cartan entry and diagram, and directly verifies B1/C1, B2/C2, D2, and D3 coincidences.
The proof now invokes root-triple existence for each simple root, maps the canonical Serre generators to those chosen triples in both algebras, and composes the resulting presentation isomorphisms.
The proof now exhibits Ax=0, observes DAD^{-1} has null vector Dx for every positive diagonal D, and uses the simple-edge Cartan constraints to show this is the unique matrix for the cycle diagram.

The Given model now uses alpha_0 and beta_0 throughout and explicitly renames the short-long ordered base by alpha=beta_0 and beta=alpha_0; the six converted positives and highest-root order then follow directly.

The double-edge calculation is now stated only for a path with exactly one multiple edge, ensuring every arm edge is simple and the common-length norm formulas apply; the later exclusion proof supplies that condition.
